cases.visibleGeometry: Broad undulating bands cross the square. A narrow north-south incised line runs near the east edge, with small breaks and rough patches near its upper half.
cases.alternatives: Drainage or track erosion; irregular roughness may be vegetation or ground-model artefacts.
cases.supportLimits: Mostly measured, with interpolation concentrated along the line and scattered rough patches; its sharpest breaks are uncertain.

cases.visibleGeometry: Closely spaced curved parallel ridges occupy the northwest corner, bounded by a diagonal linear break. The remaining ground is smooth with a few small rough spots.
cases.alternatives: Cultivation or terracing beside a track or field boundary; small spots may be vegetation effects.
cases.supportLimits: The diagonal break has substantial interpolation, so its detailed profile is uncertain; most open ground is measured.

cases.visibleGeometry: Two narrow lines meet near the northwest quadrant; one runs north-south and one trends northeast. Numerous isolated small rough circular patches occur across otherwise gently rolling ground.
cases.alternatives: Field boundaries, drainage or tracks; circular patches may mark vegetation or surface disturbance.
cases.supportLimits: The lines and many spots coincide with interpolation, limiting confidence in their shape. Most intervening ground is measured.

cases.visibleGeometry: Two near-parallel east-west linear breaks bound a broad strip. Regular fine ridges cover ground north and south; a small isolated bump lies on the northern line near x310,y100.
cases.alternatives: Field divisions, cultivation, tracks and a tree or rock bump.
cases.supportLimits: Interpolation follows both breaks and occurs at the bump, reducing profile certainty; broad fields are largely measured.

cases.visibleGeometry: Broken rough elevated forms occupy the northwest. One compact, roughly rectangular high patch around x110-175,y95-175 stands out. A large irregular missing area cuts through the southwest, and terrain drops toward the southeast.
cases.alternatives: Exposed rock, erosion, vegetation or ground-model artefacts could explain the rough patch.
cases.supportLimits: Large missing area and broad interpolated margins; the compact patch mixes measured and interpolated cells, so its outline is unreliable.

candidates.feature: Compact roughly rectangular raised rough patch
candidates.nextCheck: Inspect raw ground returns and nearby imagery for rock, vegetation and model gaps.

cases.visibleGeometry: Dense, curved parallel ridges sweep across the upper and right ground. A few irregular bumps and breaks lie near the lower centre; no isolated coherent enclosure or platform is clear.
cases.alternatives: Cultivation or terracing on slopes, with rock or vegetation affecting the lower bumps.
cases.supportLimits: Most terrain is measured; a band of interpolation overlaps the lower bumps, limiting their form.

cases.visibleGeometry: Nearly uniform fine parallel ridges cover the square, crossed by subtle broader undulations and a faint linear change near the west side. No distinct localized form stands out.
cases.alternatives: Regular cultivation furrows and a field boundary or access line.
cases.supportLimits: Measured cells dominate but fine interpolation is widespread; low-amplitude details are weak.

cases.visibleGeometry: Broad subdued slope with scattered small circular rough spots. A faint roughly horizontal line crosses the lower part, ending among rough irregular patches. No clear enclosed or stepped form.
cases.alternatives: Field boundary or track, vegetation or rocks at the spots, and slope erosion.
cases.supportLimits: Circular spots and lower rough band contain many interpolated cells; central ground is mostly measured.

cases.visibleGeometry: A large smooth oval hollow with a pronounced rim is clipped by the northeast edge. Thin straight or branching lines cross the centre and southwest; rough vertical gullies lie to the northwest. Southern edge is outside the model.
cases.alternatives: The oval could be an engineered pond or excavation; lines may be tracks, drains or field divisions.
cases.supportLimits: Most central terrain is measured. Interpolation follows rough gullies and the model boundary; the oval is clipped by the image edge.

cases.visibleGeometry: A broad diagonal route bends toward the southeast and meets a narrower branch. A separate curving low linear bank or ditch runs from west toward the junction. Small isolated bump lies in the southwest.
cases.alternatives: Road or track intersection with field boundary or drainage line; the bump could be a rock or vegetation remnant.
cases.supportLimits: Lines are mainly measured but interpolation follows the curving line; rough patches near the junction contain mixed support.

cases.visibleGeometry: Several compact raised, block-like forms cluster across the southern half, including an elongated north-south form at x120-170,y260-350 and an east-west chain at x255-395,y190-230. A curving shallow line runs between them.
cases.alternatives: Exposed bedrock, rubble, modern structures or clearance piles; the line may be a track.
cases.supportLimits: The forms are mostly on measured ground with small scattered interpolation; imagery alone cannot distinguish natural rock from constructed material.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect raw ground returns and aerial imagery for rock or standing structures.
Inspect raw returns and aerial imagery; check whether forms are connected or separate.

cases.visibleGeometry: Dense continuous curved parallel ridges fill nearly the entire square. A narrow disturbed strip appears at the far east edge; no distinct isolated geometry emerges.
cases.alternatives: Cultivation or terracing and an edge track or boundary.
cases.supportLimits: Most cells are measured with fine scattered interpolation; the east-edge disturbance has more mixed support.

cases.visibleGeometry: A straight diagonal raised route spans the upper edge. South of it lie irregular high patches, including a clipped rectangular-looking block on the west edge and rounded knobs near x110,y110. A large area outside the model truncates the east.
cases.alternatives: Road works, exposed bedrock, clearance piles or surviving structures; smooth southern ridges resemble cultivation.
cases.supportLimits: Mixed measured and interpolated cells cover rough patches. The west form and eastern terrain are clipped, preventing full outlines.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect adjacent terrain, raw returns and aerial imagery for rock or structures.

cases.visibleGeometry: A broad smooth central surface is flanked by rough incised margins. In the southeast, a sharply bounded triangular or trapezoidal raised form stands apart from smaller knobs.
cases.alternatives: Large rock outcrop or boulder, modern embankment or structure; margin lines could be drainage or tracks.
cases.supportLimits: The prominent form is mainly measured, but its adjacent margin and rough edges include interpolation. Shape alone does not establish origin.

candidates.nextCheck: Check raw point returns and aerial imagery to distinguish rock from constructed or modern material.

cases.visibleGeometry: A gently curving boundary separates rough upper ground from smoother lower ground. Scattered small bumps and a short thin line occur south of it; no coherent localized feature is evident.
cases.alternatives: Slope break, field margin, erosion and vegetation or rock patches.
cases.supportLimits: Interpolation is concentrated along the boundary and at most bumps; smooth lower ground is mostly measured.

cases.visibleGeometry: Regular narrow ridges run across most of the square and change orientation around a subtle curved middle line. A straight diagonal strip lies near the west edge. No compact feature stands out.
cases.alternatives: Cultivation patterns separated by a field margin and access strip.
cases.supportLimits: Measured terrain predominates with scattered fine interpolation; subtle crossing marks are low contrast.

cases.visibleGeometry: Several angular enclosures or levelled plots occur in the northern half, separated by a straight east-west route. A large rectangular plot with dense parallel ridges fills the south centre; more parallel rows lie at the east edge.
cases.alternatives: Active fields, orchard rows, property boundaries and modern building or yard remains may account for the geometry.
cases.supportLimits: Most plot interiors are measured; northern edges and the route have substantial mixed interpolation. One tiny missing patch lies west.

candidates.feature: Angular bounded plot with internal rectilinear relief
candidates.nextCheck: Compare raw returns and aerial imagery to identify current field or building features.
